Volume Lifecycle Support: Execute volume initialization, pool additions, data migration, volume consolidation, defragmentation, and decommission activities. Workload Safeguarding: Proactively identify and eliminate storage bottlenecks that may degrade online systems (CICS, DB2), production databases, or critical batch cycles. 2.2. IBM SL4000 Administration: Monitor, manage, and audit IBM SL4000 automated tape library environments (or equivalent enterprise tape platform). Hardware & Mount Troubleshooting: Investigate and resolve tape mount timeouts, missing/unassigned volumes, media read/ write errors, robotic arm faults, and drive hardware degradation. OEM Vendor Coordination: Coordinate tape hardware failures, drive replacements, firmware updates, and scheduled maintenance with internal infrastructure teams and OEM service vendors. 2.3. Luminex Mainframe Virtual Tape (MVT) & CGX Administration Virtual Tape Platform Support: Administer, monitor, and troubleshoot Luminex Mainframe Virtual Tape (MVT) systems and Channel Gateway (CGX) components. Throughput & Telemetry Oversight: Monitor channel availability, virtual drive states, backend SAN/NAS storage capacity, data transfer throughput, and system error logs. Operational Tooling (LTMon): Leverage Luminex operational tooling (LTMon or equivalent utilities) for message auditing, telemetry analysis, and channel health diagnostics. Replication & DR Testing: Monitor Luminex replication links, virtual tape synchronization health, recovery readiness, and participate in formal enterprise DR simulations. Media Lifecycle & Retention: Manage virtual scratch pools, VOLSER ranges, retention policies, and maintain seamless coexistence with physical tape operations. OEM Support & Configuration Governance: Coordinate patching, microcode updates, and incident resolution with Luminex Technical Support; maintain architecture diagrams, inventories, configuration records, and operational runbooks. Risk Analysis: Continuously assess single points of failure, channel latency, backend storage saturation, and replication backlog risks, recommending mitigation plans. 2.4. Production Storage Batch & Workload Collaboration Storage Abend Remediation: Rapidly triage storage-related overnight batch failures, allocation delays, and dataset lockups to ensure uninterrupted batch completion. Early-Morning Stabilization: Provide hands-on early-morning support to stabilize storage pools and tape mounts prior to business start-of-day. Workload Control Alignment: Collaborate closely with Workload Automation / Production Control personnel to remediate storage-related job halts and align dataset availability. Multi-Tier Escalation: Escalate storage issues requiring Systems Programming, RACF Security, database administration, or third-party engineering support. SECURITY, ACCESS & CHANGE GOVERNANCE RACF Compliance: Operate strictly within established RACF security profiles, dataset protection rules, and privileged access protocols. Operational Coordination: Maintain thorough comprehension of RACF security dependencies to safely coordinate storage volume maintenance without disrupting running workloads. ITIL Alignment: Adhere to enterprise ITIL processes for Change, Incident, and Problem Management; document RCAs and participate in change implementation reviews. Storage Software: Advanced proficiency with DFSMS (DFSMSdfp, DFSMSdss, DFSMShsm, DFSMSrmm/CA-1), IDCAMS, and catalog management utilities. Storage Hardware: Hands-on operational mastery of enterprise DASD storage arrays, IBM SL4000 automated tape libraries, and Luminex Virtual Tape (MVT/CGX/LTMon). Operating Environment: Strong competency with TSO/ISPF, SDSF, JCL, and JES2 commands. Incident Governance: Proven experience adhering to enterprise ITIL incident management SLAs (e.g., ServiceNow).
